idiom_name: std::variant actions + pure reduce() over value states + std::function subscribers
implementation_notes: Modern C++ supplies the pieces but no framework: actions are std::variant alternatives, the reducer is a pure function (typically std::visit over an exhaustive overload set), immutable snapshots are moved value objects or std::shared_ptr<const State>, and subscribers are std::function slots (or a Boost.Signals2/Qt signal when a framework is already present). Value semantics plus const enforce more of the discipline than in C - a reducer receives const State& and returns a new State - but a shared_ptr<State> published to views and mutated through bypasses it entirely, so publish immutable snapshots and copy along the changed path. Hand-writing remains the norm because no dominant C++ Flux/Redux framework exists; the classic form is justified for immediate-mode UIs (Dear ImGui-style) and for test harnesses that replay actions, not for a single view that can own its own state.
pitfalls: A non-const shared_ptr<State> held by both the store and the views recreates aliasing; publish shared_ptr<const State> and copy-modify-replace inside the reducer.
Subscriber slots capturing a raw this pointer of a destroyed widget keep firing; use weak ownership (weak_ptr + lock) or scoped signal connections and disconnect on destruction.
A visitor with a generic auto fallback silently swallows newly added alternatives; keep std::visit exhaustive so a new action type fails to compile.
Dispatch from several threads needs an explicit policy - serialise it behind a mutex or queue, or keep the store single-threaded and marshal actions to its executor.
